title: Sharing among friends
competency: Use rational numbers to share things fairly.

keywords.def: To divide something into equal parts for several people.

en.text: When something is shared equally, each person gets the whole divided by the number of people. If part is taken first, find what is left, then divide that.

am.text: አንድ ነገር በእኩል ሲካፈል እያንዳንዱ ሙሉውን በሰዎች ቁጥር ተካፍሎ ያገኛል። መጀመሪያ ክፍል ከተወሰደ የቀረውን ፈልገህ አካፍል።

screens.ask: Four friends share one cake equally. Each gets
screens.after:
One cake is cut into 4 equal parts, one for each friend.
Each friend gets 1 part of 4: 1/4 of the cake.
1 ÷ 4 = 1/4. (4 and 4/1 would be four whole cakes each!)

screens.title: One cake, four friends
screens.after:
The cake is cut into 4 equal parts.
Each friend gets 1 part: 1 ÷ 4 = 1/4.
4 × 1/4 = 1 whole cake.

screens.title: 1.4 Real life applications
paras: We use rational numbers for sharing, loans and savings.
We also use them for discounts, prices and budgets.

screens.title: Example 1.34: the sugarcane
paras: Three brothers buy sugarcane. Their mother takes a fifth.
The brothers share the rest equally. What fraction does each get?

screens.after: Each brother gets 1/5 + 1/15 = 4/15. The mother keeps 3/15 = 1/5.

screens.title: Solution
steps: Cut the sugarcane into 5 equal big pieces. Each big piece is 1/5.
The mother takes 1 big piece. 4 big pieces are left.
Each brother takes 1 big piece: 1/5 each. That uses 3 pieces.
1 big piece is still left. Cut it into 3 equal parts: 1/5 ÷ 3 = 1/5 × 1/3 = 1/15.

screens.title: Share
defs: To divide something into equal parts for several people.

screens.text: Sharing the sugarcane: why does each brother get an extra 1/15?
screens.why:
After each brother takes 1/5, one big piece (1/5) is left.
It is shared by 3 brothers: 1/5 ÷ 3.
1/5 ÷ 3 = 1/5 × 1/3 = 1/15.
So each brother gets an extra 1/15.
screens.clue: Look at the last big piece.

screens.ask: Share by dividing: five friends share 2 injera equally. Each gets ___ injera.
screens.why:
Share means divide: 2 ÷ 5.
2 ÷ 5 = 2/5.
As a decimal, 2/5 = 0.4.
Check: 5 × 2/5 = 10/5 = 2 injera.

screens.ask: Share a fraction: three brothers share 3/4 kg of coffee equally. Each gets ___ kg.
screens.why:
Share means divide: 3/4 ÷ 3.
Dividing by 3 is multiplying by 1/3: 3/4 × 1/3 = 3/12.
Divide top and bottom by 3: 1/4 kg.
Check: 3 × 1/4 = 3/4.

screens.ask: Fraction of a group: Eleni baked 32 cupcakes and iced 24. Fraction iced = ___
screens.why:
Fraction iced = iced ÷ total = 24/32.
The GCF of 24 and 32 is 8.
24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 32 ÷ 8 = 4.
So 3/4 of the cupcakes are iced.

screens.ask: Share in steps: father takes 1/4 of a cake. Mother takes 1/3 of what is left. 2 children share the rest equally. Each child gets ___ of the cake.
screens.why:
After father: 1 − 1/4 = 3/4 is left.
Mother takes 1/3 of 3/4 = 1/3 × 3/4 = 3/12 = 1/4.
Left now: 3/4 − 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.
Each child: 1/2 ÷ 2 = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.
Check: 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1 whole cake.
screens.clue: Go step by step: what is left after each person?

items.ask: Share by dividing: six students share 4 loaves of bread equally. Each gets ___ loaf.
items.why:
Share means divide: 4 ÷ 6 = 4/6.
The GCF of 4 and 6 is 2.
4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
Each student gets 2/3 of a loaf.

items.ask: Share what is left: a mother takes 1/4 of a cake. 3 children share the rest. Each child gets ___
items.why:
Left after the mother: 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.
Share by 3: 3/4 ÷ 3 = 3/4 × 1/3 = 3/12.
Divide top and bottom by 3: 1/4.
Each child gets 1/4 of the cake.

items.ask: Fraction of a group: Eleni iced 24 of 32 cupcakes. Fraction iced = ___
items.why:
Fraction iced = 24/32.
The GCF of 24 and 32 is 8.
24 ÷ 8 = 3 and 32 ÷ 8 = 4.
Answer: 3/4.

test.ask: Share what is left: a mother takes 1/3 of a sugarcane. 2 brothers share the rest. Each gets ___
test.why:
Left after the mother: 1 − 1/3 = 2/3.
Share by 2: 2/3 ÷ 2 = 2/3 × 1/2 = 2/6.
Divide top and bottom by 2: 1/3.
Each brother gets 1/3.

test.ask: Share by dividing: eight friends share 3 pizzas. Each gets ___ pizza.
Share by dividing: four friends share 3 injera equally. Each gets ___ injera.
Share what is left: mother takes 1/3 of a cake; 4 children share the rest. Each gets ___
test.why:
Left after the mother: 1 − 1/3 = 2/3.
Share by 4: 2/3 ÷ 4 = 2/3 × 1/4 = 2/12.
Divide top and bottom by 2: 1/6.

test.ask: Share in steps: father takes 1/5, mother takes 1/4 of what is left, 3 children share the rest. Each child gets ___

notes.text: The book has no exercise for 1.4.1; Practice 1.4.1 is added (marked added). Review Exercise Q9 is used here.
